predictions.reason: Assessment for secondary infection or PE remains clinically necessary regardless of pregnancy status.
Evaluation for ARDS, IRIS, or superimposed infection remains equally critical in pregnancy.
ABC assessment is a universal emergency priority unaffected by pregnancy status.
Respiratory support escalation thresholds and modalities remain standard despite pregnancy.
Lung-protective ventilation principles apply universally post-intubation.
WHO MDR-TB guidelines remain the reference standard; pregnancy modifies drug selection but not the criterion's core requirement.
IV isoniazid remains safe and indicated for severe TB regardless of pregnancy.
Corticosteroid indications for severe TB complications do not change with pregnancy.
Emergency transfer for ABC compromise is universally indicated.
Airborne precautions for drug-resistant TB are mandatory regardless of pregnancy.
Unjustified broad-spectrum antibiotics remain clinically inappropriate in any patient.
Sedation indications for respiratory distress remain unchanged.
Escalation to rapid response or ICU remains a critical safety step.
Oxygen escalation to HFNC or NIV remains standard for refractory hypoxemia.
Starting with ABCs is a fundamental emergency protocol.
Intubation consideration for failed non-invasive support remains standard.
Airborne precautions are infection control standards unaffected by pregnancy.
Objective data collection including shielded CXR remains standard and safe.
ID consultation remains essential for complex MDR-TB management.
Broadening antibiotics without sensitivity data remains inappropriate.
Premature extensive ARDS management discussion remains discouraged without data.
Failure to escalate to RRT or ICU remains a critical safety omission.
General response quality and emergency referral standards remain unchanged.
Relevance, correctness, and efficiency standards remain unchanged.

proposed_induced: Recommends a pregnancy-safe MDR-TB regimen per WHO guidelines, explicitly avoiding or cautioning against teratogenic/unsafe agents (e.g., fluoroquinolones, aminoglycosides, bedaquiline) unless benefits strictly outweigh risks.
Advises OB/GYN or Maternal-Fetal Medicine consultation for coordinated management of MDR-TB during the first trimester.
Specifies radiation safety measures for imaging (e.g., abdominal shielding for CXR, deferring CT unless absolutely necessary, considering V/Q scan or ultrasound for PE).
Acknowledges pregnancy-related physiological changes (e.g., increased oxygen consumption, reduced functional residual capacity) when interpreting respiratory decline and setting oxygenation targets.
Recommends high-dose folic acid supplementation alongside isoniazid therapy to support fetal neural tube development.
